content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The text adjudicates exactly the collision K-C governs: the witnesses [DR3] presses against the defender's Isaiah 7:14 link are the challenger's own chain read together (Link 6 footed on Isaiah 7:14, 7:16, 8:3-4, 8:8), which [CR2] answers with the defender's own chain (8:8, 9:6-7).", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the sign itself does not state the mechanism.", "rule_words": "the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side", "room": "The definition's phrase 'never the deciding test, for or against' together with K-C's 'for either side': reading one, the ban reaches only verdicts decided for or against a side, so resting an UNDERDETERMINED finding on a verse's silence escapes it; reading two, a single verse's silence can carry no verdict at all in a chain-against-chain collision, non-determination included. I weighed reading two, because the judge's stated ground for UNDERDETERMINED is wholly the sign's silence and the text offers no footing-weighing of the two chains.", "why": "The judge let one verse's silence -- the sign's failure to state the mechanism -- carry the verdict instead of weighing the defender's chain against the challenger's chain by footing, which is the stating-verse test K-C retires at a judge's seat for either side."}
